title: Potato and Sauerkraut Dumplings with Caramelised Onions
summary: A soft sour-cream dough is filled with riced potato beaten with chopped sauerkraut and butter, boiled until the dumplings float, then turned in a pan of slow-cooked golden onions and served with sour cream and chives.
equipment: 7.5 cm round cutter or a glass
2 trays and a clean tea towel

ingredients.item: plain flour, plus extra for dusting
fine sea salt or table salt
cold water (up to 4 tbsp if needed)
floury potatoes (such as Maris Piper or russet), peeled and cut into 3 cm chunks
sauerkraut, well drained, squeezed dry and finely chopped
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Make the dough
steps.text: Mix flour, salt, egg, sour cream and butter into a soft dough, knead briefly and rest 30 minutes.

steps.title: Make the filling
steps.text: Boil and rice the potatoes, then beat in the sauerkraut, butter, white pepper and salt and chill.

steps.title: Cook the onions
steps.text: Cook the onion slowly in butter for 15-20 minutes until deep golden.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: Roll the dough thin, cut rounds, fill and pinch into sealed half-moons.

steps.title: Boil
steps.text: Cook in batches in unsalted boiling water until they float, then 2-3 minutes more.

steps.title: Fry and serve
steps.text: Turn the pierogi in the onion pan with a splash of cooking water until golden, and serve with sour cream and chives.

tips: Squeeze the sauerkraut hard; wet filling makes the edges hard to seal.
Keep unused dough wrapped so it does not dry out.
Freeze some uncooked on a tray for a quick supper later.
storage: Refrigerate cooked pierogi up to 3 days and pan-fry to reheat until piping hot. Freeze uncooked pierogi up to 3 months and boil from frozen. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
